Can I trust the table? Gaussians for Raman bands: Raman bands are Lorentzian. The reduced chi-squared of 4936 unweighted tells me little. The report may give caveats. File, Export, Report.

events.target: opened the report in a browser tab

events.text: The report is a proper record: fingerprint of the raw data, both steps with settings, both fits with the processing each was made on, a timestamped list. So I can explain every step. Whether to trust the table: it has no notes or warnings at all. It doesn't say the fit is unweighted with chi-squared 4936 or that the residuals spike at the 1001 band, and it doesn't say anything about Gaussians for Raman bands. Provenance yes, judgement no; I would ask for Lorentzian or Voigt shapes and a look at the residuals.

The report records provenance completely (raw fingerprint, steps and settings, fit history with the processing of each, timestamped actions) but gives the reader no quality verdict: no notes for this fit, reduced χ² of 4936 unexplained, residual structure at the strongest band not mentioned.
The report's figure is panel (a) only at the top, then the whole figure under 'All graphs'; both panels show the fitted spectrum, not raw and fitted as built.

events.note: every step explained from the History, the Log and the report; trust judged by the reader's own expertise (Gaussian shapes for Raman, unweighted, residual structure) since the app offers no verdict

events.target: Deliberately misuse: fit with 2 points, import a broken file, type text in a number column

events.text: (Persona A again) Let's break things. First the file my labmate sent, results.csv.

'Looks like a binary instrument file. Export it as CSV from the instrument software.' It's from Excel, not an instrument. Still, I get it: save it as CSV properly. Now a fit with two points. New project from the arrow by the name.

An Excel workbook renamed .csv is refused as 'a binary instrument file … export it from the instrument software': the right refusal, the wrong remedy for an .xlsx (save as CSV from Excel; or read xlsx).
A new project, but the maximised History is still filling the screen ('1 spectrum', 'No data yet'). Open the worksheet from the taskbar.
A new project inherits the previous project's maximised History window; its title says '1 spectrum' while the body says 'No data yet'.
Two points: (1, 2) and (2, 3.5). Then a word in the number column.
about four
What happened? I typed into the worksheet and the graph came up, and the project name is selected for renaming. My numbers went nowhere.

After bringing the worksheet forward from the taskbar, cell A1 shows as selected but does not take typing: the keys went elsewhere (the graph came to the front and the project name opened for renaming).
Nothing was typed. Click in the cell first this time.
about four
Clear: 'not a number, type one or press Esc'. The cell stays red with my text. Esc. Now fit a Gaussian peak to two points, just to see.
'Fits 2 unmasked points.' Four parameters, two points. The Fit button doesn't object. Press it.
'Need more than 4 points to fit 4 free parameters (have 2).' Fair and clear, though the Fit button looked fine before I pressed it. Now a straight line on two points.
Two points, a straight line: refused, 'need more than 2 points'. Excel would draw that line and call R squared 1. I understand why not, but nothing offers to just draw the line through them.

A straight line through exactly two points is refused ('need more than 2 points to fit 2 free parameters'); Excel draws it. Defensible, but the message gives no way forward (e.g. no errors can be computed, the line is exact).
The Fit button gives no warning before it is pressed: a model with more parameters than points is only refused after Fit.

events.note: each misuse refused with a message in words and recovered from: binary file (wrong remedy for an xlsx), text in a number cell (kept, red, Esc), too few points (refused after Fit); a new hazard: keys typed after bringing the worksheet forward went to shortcuts
